find: A session waiting for a grant keeps thinking and editing; only its next build, test or proof waits. When the Mac's single bay pair is held, a second Mac session's proof waits for it or runs on the Spark by remote lane. The limits are the starting values T5 sets, and each test number is a ceiling (#2924): the first test grant always starts, and each one past it only while the memory available, less 24 GiB for each test grant still settling (under 5 minutes old), still leaves 24 GiB for one more capped run, without the load (section 6, #3694). That is the Spark, whose runs are units capped at 24 GiB. The Mac reads the memory available from `kern.memorystatus_level`, and budgets 8 GiB a run in place of the 24 (#2980). An `affected.mjs` run's test grant is its admission, decided by the same rules and only while the disk holds room for its shards above the floor; once admitted, its jobs take turns with every other admitted run's on the pool of job tokens, a token to the run whose jobs have had the least time so far, and never more of their jobs or compiles run at once than the pool (#3221, section 6). A plain test request is admitted the same way and takes a turn as a run of one job (#3694). The trust this gives up: none in what a test proves, since a job still runs alone in its shard; a run's time depends on the runs beside it, as it already did through the load; and an admitted run holds its shards' disk while it waits its turn. The build number is a ceiling too (#3549): a build asked for under no grant is admitted as a run is, the first always and each one past it only while fewer than the ceiling are held and the memory available, less a run's for each build still settling, leaves a run's memory for one more, without the load. An admitted build then takes a turn on the same pool, a run of one job, and its compiles draw on the pool. The trust that gives up: none in what a build produces, since each cargo builds in its own checkout's `target/`; a build's time depends on the builds and runs beside it; and several builds hold memory at once, which the memory rule admits them by. A change to any of these is a change to `throttle.mjs` and needs a signed approval tag.
